define.summary: Define the 2026-season championship, even if its scheduled date changes. Use official NFL results; cancellation without a champion is void.

question.text: Will the New England Patriots be the official winner of Super Bowl LXI, the championship game for the 2026 NFL season?
question.yes: The NFL's official final result names the New England Patriots as winner of Super Bowl LXI.
question.no: The NFL's official final result names another team as winner of Super Bowl LXI.
question.void: No official winner is declared by 2027-03-31T23:59:59Z, including cancellation or an unresolved final-result dispute.
question.rescheduling: Follow the named championship if rescheduled within the resolution deadline.

prior.summary: Compute the previous-runner-up reference class for seasons 2000–2024: one of 25 won the following championship, a raw 4% frequency.

payload.rationale: The target team is a returning runner-up. Use the last 25 eligible season pairs as a transparent descriptive class; its small size, repeated franchises, and changing rosters limit predictive value.

drivers.summary: Map the nested title path; elicit component probabilities later using the research coverage, with no independence assumption.

drivers.event: Win the AFC conditional on reaching the playoffs
Win the Super Bowl conditional on winning the AFC

payload.probability_identity: P(title)=P(playoffs)*P(AFC title|playoffs)*P(Super Bowl win|AFC title). Conditional on a completed competition.
unestimated: No season-and-seeding simulation; component probabilities will be labeled judgments.

market.summary: Read the complete BetUS board and a Covers comparison. Preserve table/prose disagreement and the unverified higher comparison quote; these automatically request reconciliation.

conflicts.detail: Use of +1800 versus +2000 changes the implied probability; the page does not establish which quote was updated last.

reconcile.summary: Obtain a second complete primary board. Use each table consistently, exclude the unsupported comparison from numerical pooling, and retain unknown timing as a limitation.

update.summary: Elicit 70% to reach the playoffs, 18% to win the AFC conditional on qualification, and 48% to win the Super Bowl conditional on winning the AFC. Product: 6.048%.

playoffs.rationale: More likely than not to qualify given last-season performance and QB continuity; allow substantial regression, stronger competition and health uncertainty. 70% is elicited, not estimated from historical data.

afc_given_playoffs.rationale: Conditional on qualifying, consider New England a credible but non-dominant conference contender. Difficult seeding/matchups and line performance temper the estimate; 18% is a judgment.

title_given_afc.rationale: Reaching the final selects for a successful Patriots season. Use near-even chances against an unknown NFC champion, modestly tempered by demonstrated protection risk. 48% is a judgment.

payload.rationale: Form an explicit football assessment from the recorded evidence and compare with the earlier market baseline afterward. These judgments were made with prior awareness of the odds, so the result is not a blind forecast.
limitations: Parameters are subjective and unfitted; linked facts do not uniquely imply the selected numbers.
Market prices were already seen, leaving anchoring possible.
Several sources are team-authored analysis rather than independent causal evaluation.
No new post-market private information has been established.
No numerical player/coaching bonuses are added to already informed market prices.
Assumes the championship completes; cancellation follows the question's void policy.

review.summary: Retain a rounded 6% working judgment, while treating 2.88%–11% as scenario sensitivity, not a statistical interval or demonstrated market edge.

objections.objection: Last-season wins and QB statistics may exaggerate repeatable strength without opponent adjustment.
objections.response: The 70% qualification estimate already allows substantial regression; test a 60% alternative. A fitted team-strength model remains a material gap.

objections.objection: A.J. Brown is not a pure addition to an otherwise unchanged offense.
objections.response: Keep the Diggs departure, line changes and other turnover in the same assessment; no standalone Brown percentage-point bonus is applied.

objections.objection: A strong young quarterback, continuity and better receiving options could support a higher ceiling.
objections.response: Evaluate the optimistic conditional assumptions explicitly rather than treating upside as the central case.

objections.objection: The conditional probabilities are subjective and may reflect the already-seen market.
objections.response: Label the model as elicited and not blind; a small numerical difference from the market is not a validated edge.

objections.objection: The runner-up reference class has only one success and repeated franchises.
objections.response: Use it as descriptive context and show recent-window sensitivity; do not treat 4% as a precise prior or average it as independent evidence.

payload.rationale: Keep the explicit 6.048% scenario as a rounded 6% working judgment. The uncertainty in the assumptions matters more than the extra decimal places.

check.summary: Check the conditional product, nested event bounds, source references, and market calculations.

issue.summary: Issue a separate researched demonstration forecast at 6.048%, pinning new findings and elicited assumptions. Preserve the earlier market-baseline record.

payload.stopping_reason: Required football research domains have been addressed. Issue a tentative, uncalibrated elicitation with parameter sensitivity; specialist team-rating and season-simulation work remain explicit limitations.

triggers.instruction: Acquire comparable timestamped complete boards; recalculate and review.
Assess material changes in availability; avoid automatic numerical adjustments.
After the opening game, review new prices, team performance, and injuries without treating one game as the full season.
Resolve only with an official final championship result under the original question criteria.
Review pass-protection performance and Maye efficiency against strong defenses; revise the relevant conditional assumptions.

fundamentals.summary: Collect last-season strength, quarterback performance, coaching continuity, roster gains and losses, line concerns, schedule context, and historical championship results.

findings.claim: The 2025 regular season ended 14–3, with 490 points scored and 320 allowed.
Maye's 2025 regular-season passing line was 4,394 yards, 31 touchdowns and 8 interceptions.
McDaniels remains offensive coordinator in 2026 after returning in 2025.
Kuhr becomes defensive coordinator after already assuming play-calling in 2025.
New England acquired A.J. Brown on June 1, 2026.
Diggs was released and Bradbury traded; Brown joins a changed offense.
Arrivals include Doubs, Byard and Dre'Mont Jones; departures include Chaisson and Tonga.
The Super Bowl loss included six sacks and heavy pressure; the 2026 line has personnel changes.
The 2026 schedule includes several difficult away assignments and Detroit in Munich.
The 2025 schedule looked favorable using opponents' 2024 records; that measure is not a realized 2025 adjustment.
New England was runner-up for the 2025 season, making prior runners-up a candidate reference class.

prior_performance.interpretation: A strong season and title-game appearance establish contention, but raw results are not opponent-adjusted and the comparable cohort is small.

quarterback.interpretation: Elite regular-season production supports a high ceiling. The playoff protection failure limits confidence against elite opponents.

coaching.interpretation: Treat coaching as continuity, not two new-coach upgrades; title changes alone are not incremental performance.

roster_changes.interpretation: Brown and other arrivals create upside, while departures, fit, line health and defensive turnover prevent a simple additions-only adjustment.

schedule.interpretation: The road slate and travel temper assumptions about repeating the record and securing advantageous seeding. Prior-year opponent records are an imperfect measure.
